ground_truth.description: The suppression check relies on semantic/vector search (`search(query="stage1_flag_suppression", ...)`) to locate a specific task's suppression record. Vector search returns only a bounded top-k ranked by similarity, so when suppression records exist for many tasks (or the corpus is large), the record for the target task_id may not appear in the results at all. The check then concludes 'no suppression in effect' and emits the flag — a false negative that exactly matches the flagged symptom (review passed but escalation_created). A deterministic metadata lookup (e.g. get_memories_by_metadata / count_memories_by_metadata filtered on kind+task_id) is required.

The search query string is the generic literal "stage1_flag_suppression" and does not include the target task_id, so records for all other tasks compete for the limited top-k slots and can crowd out the relevant task's record, again causing the target's suppression to be missed.

The validity test requires `metadata.task_id == <N>` as an integer, but metadata persisted through Mem0 may store the task_id as a string; a strict integer equality check would then reject a genuine suppression record and fall through to emitting the flag (false negative). The comparison should be type-normalized.

task.title: Stage 1 system prompt: add pre-emission suppression check before writing any stage1_flag_marker for task 452
task.description: Stage 1 (memory_consolidator) must search for active suppression records BEFORE emitting any stage1_flag_marker for task 452. Without this check, Stage 1 may write violating markers even when suppression is active, requiring repeated remediation runs to delete them. Four violations have occurred across cycles 38, 39, 51, and potentially future cycles.
task.details:
Root cause: Stage 1 flag-dedup logic writes new markers for tasks without first checking if a suppression record exists that prohibits emission. For task 452 (autopilot_video: 'Investigate 2026-04-21 mass task reset', status=deferred since 2026-04-27), two authoritative suppression memories exist: mem0:87643d99 and mem0:ff84b3fb (autopilot_video project). 

Fix required: At the start of the flag-emission loop in Stage 1 system prompt, add a step: "Before writing any stage1_flag_marker, search for active suppression records for the target task_id. If a suppression record exists and the task remains in the suppressed status, skip flag emission." This prevents the contamination cycle where Stage 1 writes a violating flag → Stage 3 detects it → remediation run deletes it → next cycle Stage 1 writes it again.

Suppression enforcement memories (autopilot_video project):
- 87643d99-57b1-40e7-a62c-3b36481bb2cb: STAGE 1 FLAG SUPPRESSION directive for task 452
- ff84b3fb-715e-4e65-a444-94b3bd2050fa: STAGE 1 FLAG SUPPRESSION UPDATE (cycle-51 violation cleanup)

The fix applies to the Stage 1 system prompt in the dark-factory reconciliation harness, specifically the pre-emission check step.
